title: TLS/SSL
subtitle: The TLS handshake, cipher suites, and HTTPS

content.text: TLS (Transport Layer Security) encrypts data in transit between client and server. TLS 1.3 is the current version; TLS 1.0/1.1 are deprecated.

content.code:
TLS 1.3 Handshake (simplified):
1. Client Hello  — supported cipher suites, random nonce
2. Server Hello  — chosen cipher, certificate, key share (ECDH)
3. Client        — verifies certificate, sends key share
4. Both sides    — derive symmetric session keys from ECDH shared secret
5. All data      — encrypted with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305

import ssl, socket

context = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
context.minimum_version = ssl.TLSVersion.TLSv1_2
context.load_cert_chain("cert.pem", "key.pem")

with socket.socket() as sock:
    sock.bind(("localhost", 4443))
    sock.listen(1)
    with context.wrap_socket(sock, server_side=True) as ssock:
        conn, addr = ssock.accept()
        data = conn.recv(1024)
        conn.send(b"Hello over TLS!")

questions.question: What does TLS protect against?
options: Eavesdropping and tampering of data in transit
questions.explanation: TLS encrypts and authenticates data in transit between client and server, preventing eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks.

faq.a: HTTP Strict Transport Security — a header that tells browsers to only connect via HTTPS for a specified duration, preventing protocol downgrade attacks.
